faq.q: Does the shortener work without a backend?
faq.a: The actual short link is created by the third-party is.gd API, because a static page can't host redirects itself. The Shorten tab sends your long URL to is.gd (disclosed on the page) and returns a real is.gd short link, saving the last 5 in your browser. The other six tabs — UTM builder, URL parser, tracker cleaner, encoder, safety check, and QR — run entirely in your browser with no requests.

faq.q: What does the Tracker Cleaner remove?
faq.a: It strips a defined list of tracking parameters: all utm_* variants, plus fbclid, gclid, dclid, gclsrc, msclkid, igshid, mc_eid, mc_cid, ref, yclid, twclid, li_fat_id, _ga and more. It also removes any parameter whose name starts with utm_. It then shows the cleaned URL and lists exactly which parameters were removed, or says none were found.

faq.q: Is the Safety Check a malware scanner?
faq.a: No — it's explicitly heuristic, not a scanner, and a clean result doesn't guarantee safety. It flags things you can eyeball: http instead of https, a raw IP host, punycode (xn--) that can indicate a lookalike domain, excessive subdomains, abuse-prone TLDs (like .tk, .xyz, .top, .zip), very long/obfuscated paths, and percent-encoding in the hostname.

faq.q: Can the UTM builder and QR code help with campaigns?
faq.a: Yes. The UTM builder has channel presets (Google Ads, Facebook, Instagram, email, YouTube, WhatsApp, LinkedIn) that fill source and medium, builds a properly encoded URL live, and lets you save campaigns (up to 20, under utmCampaigns). The QR tab generates a scannable code for any link using a UTF-8-aware encoder so Hindi, the rupee sign, or accents scan correctly, and downloads it as a PNG.
